title: First Impressions & Verb To Be
grammar_focus: Verb 'to be' (am/is/are), subject pronouns, basic wh-questions
desc: Introduce yourself, say where you are from, and ask basic personal questions.
warmup_prompt: How are you feeling today? Where are you from?
roleplay_scenario: Meeting a friendly new coworker on your first day at an international office.
objectives: Use 'I'm', 'you're', and 'my name is' naturally
Ask and answer 'Where are you from?' and 'What do you do?'
Practice contracted forms without dropping the verb 'to be'
communicative_function: Introduce yourself, say where you are from, and ask basic personal questions.

title: My Daily Routine
grammar_focus: Present Simple (affirmative, negative, 3rd person -s)
vocabulary_focus: Daily habits, morning/evening actions, times of day
desc: Describe your typical weekday and ask someone about their daily schedule.
warmup_prompt: What time do you usually wake up?
roleplay_scenario: Chatting with a language partner about your morning and work routines.
objectives: Describe 4+ daily activities using Present Simple
Use 'don't' and 'doesn't' correctly in negatives
Tell the time and use 'at' with specific times
communicative_function: Describe your typical weekday and ask someone about their daily schedule.

title: At the Café & Restaurant
grammar_focus: 'I'd like...', 'Can I have...?', There is / There are
desc: Order food and drinks politely and ask about menu items.
warmup_prompt: What is your favorite coffee or breakfast food?
roleplay_scenario: Ordering breakfast and asking about ingredients at a busy London café.
objectives: Order using 'I'd like' or 'Can I have' instead of 'I want'
Ask 'Is there...?' or 'Do you have...?'
Understand prices and pay politely
communicative_function: Order food and drinks politely and ask about menu items.

title: Family, Friends & Possessives
grammar_focus: Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her) & possessive 's
desc: Talk about your family members, their ages, and what they are like.
warmup_prompt: Do you have a big family or a small family?
roleplay_scenario: Showing a friend photos of your family and describing who is who.
objectives: Use 'his', 'her', and 'their' accurately
Use possessive 's (e.g., my sister's job)
Describe people with 3+ adjectives
communicative_function: Talk about your family members, their ages, and what they are like.

title: Around Town & Directions
grammar_focus: Imperatives, prepositions of place (next to, across from, between)
pronunciation_focus: Word stress in compound nouns (bus stop, train station)
desc: Ask where places are and understand simple walking directions.
warmup_prompt: Is there a good park or café near your house?
roleplay_scenario: Asking a local for directions to the nearest subway station and pharmacy.
objectives: Ask 'Excuse me, how do I get to...?'
Use 'next to', 'opposite', and 'on the corner'
Confirm directions by repeating key landmarks
communicative_function: Ask where places are and understand simple walking directions.

title: Abilities & Weekend Plans
grammar_focus: Modal 'can / can't' for ability and permission; Present Continuous for now
desc: Talk about what you can do well and what you are doing right now.
warmup_prompt: What is one thing you can do very well?
roleplay_scenario: Planning a casual weekend hangout with a friend.
objectives: Contrast 'can' and 'can't' clearly in speech
Ask 'Can you...?' questions naturally
Describe current actions using Present Continuous
communicative_function: Talk about what you can do well and what you are doing right now.

title: Yesterday & Life Stories (Past Simple)
grammar_focus: Past Simple: regular (-ed) and irregular verbs, 'did/didn't' questions
vocabulary_focus: Time expressions (yesterday, last week, two days ago), common irregular verbs
desc: Tell stories about yesterday, your last trip, or your weekend using accurate past verbs.
warmup_prompt: What did you do last weekend?
roleplay_scenario: Catching up on Monday morning and sharing what happened over the weekend.
objectives: Use at least 5 irregular Past Simple verbs correctly (went, saw, bought, ate, had)
Form negatives and questions with 'didn't' + base verb
Pronounce -ed endings cleanly without adding an extra syllable unnecessarily
communicative_function: Tell stories about yesterday, your last trip, or your weekend using accurate past verbs.

title: Interrupted Moments (Past Continuous)
grammar_focus: Past Continuous vs. Past Simple with 'when' and 'while'
desc: Explain what was happening in the background when something unexpected occurred.
warmup_prompt: What were you doing at 8 PM last night?
roleplay_scenario: Explaining to a friend why you missed their phone call yesterday.
objectives: Combine Past Continuous and Past Simple ('I was cooking when you called')
Use 'while' and 'when' accurately
Use weak vowel sounds in 'was' and 'were'
communicative_function: Explain what was happening in the background when something unexpected occurred.

title: Future Plans & Instant Decisions
grammar_focus: 'Be going to' (intentions/plans) vs. 'Will' (instant decisions/offers/predictions)
vocabulary_focus: Upcoming projects, travel plans, promises, weather
desc: Talk about your upcoming plans and react to situations with spontaneous offers.
warmup_prompt: What are you going to do after this English class?
roleplay_scenario: Organizing a surprise dinner party with a friend and dividing tasks on the spot.
objectives: Use 'going to' for plans already decided
Use 'I'll...' for spontaneous offers and decisions
Ask future questions naturally
communicative_function: Talk about your upcoming plans and react to situations with spontaneous offers.

title: Comparing Cities, Tech & Choices
grammar_focus: Comparatives & Superlatives (-er/-est, more/most, irregular: better/worse, as...as)
vocabulary_focus: City life, technology, quality adjectives, price/speed
desc: Compare two cities, products, or lifestyles and explain which one is the best.
warmup_prompt: Is your city bigger or quieter than the capital?
roleplay_scenario: Helping a friend choose between two apartments or two laptops.
objectives: Avoid 'more better' — use 'much better' and 'far worse'
Contrast short adjectives (-er) with long adjectives (more + adj)
Use 'the best / the most...' superlatives in recommendations
communicative_function: Compare two cities, products, or lifestyles and explain which one is the best.

title: Shopping, Quantities & Returning Items
grammar_focus: Countable/Uncountable nouns, some/any, much/many, a lot of, a few/a little
pronunciation_focus: Connected speech in 'a lot of' and 'how much'
desc: Handle shopping, ask for quantities, and politely return or exchange a faulty item.
warmup_prompt: How much coffee do you drink every day?
roleplay_scenario: Returning a jacket that is the wrong size at a clothing store.
objectives: Use 'How much' (uncountable) vs 'How many' (countable) accurately
Use 'some' in offers/requests and 'any' in negatives/questions
Politely ask for a refund or a different size
communicative_function: Handle shopping, ask for quantities, and politely return or exchange a faulty item.

title: Rules, Obligations & Travel Advice
grammar_focus: Modals: have to, don't have to, must, mustn't, should/shouldn't
vocabulary_focus: Airport rules, workplace policies, travel tips
desc: Explain what is required, optional, or prohibited in travel and work situations.
warmup_prompt: What do you have to do every morning before starting work?
roleplay_scenario: Briefing a foreign colleague visiting your country/office for the first time.
objectives: Distinguish 'don't have to' (not necessary) from 'mustn't' (prohibited)
Give friendly recommendations using 'should / shouldn't'
Pronounce 'have to' naturally without over-stressing
communicative_function: Explain what is required, optional, or prohibited in travel and work situations.

title: Prepositions of Time & Place Mastery
grammar_focus: Prepositions: in, on, at (time, dates, locations, transport)
vocabulary_focus: Calendar dates, schedules, addresses, digital media
pronunciation_focus: Linking prepositions to following words (at eight, on Monday)
desc: Eliminate the most common Portuguese-speaker mistake with 'in', 'on', and 'at'.
warmup_prompt: When is your birthday, and what time were you born?
roleplay_scenario: Scheduling a doctor's appointment and confirming meeting details.
objectives: Use 'at' for exact times, 'on' for days/dates, 'in' for months/years/parts of day
Use 'at home / at work', 'on the bus / on the internet', 'in the city'
Self-correct preposition slips when prompted
communicative_function: Eliminate the most common Portuguese-speaker mistake with 'in', 'on', and 'at'.

title: Health, Doctor Visits & Describing Pain
grammar_focus: 'I've had...' (intro), 'It hurts', giving instructions & advice
vocabulary_focus: Body parts, symptoms (headache, fever, sore throat), remedies
desc: Describe how you feel at a pharmacy or doctor's office and understand advice.
warmup_prompt: What do you usually do when you have a cold?
roleplay_scenario: Visiting a pharmacy abroad to explain symptoms and buy medicine.
objectives: Describe symptoms clearly ('I have a sore throat / My back hurts')
Ask about dosage ('How often should I take this?')
Understand instructions and warnings
communicative_function: Describe how you feel at a pharmacy or doctor's office and understand advice.

title: Storytelling with Connectors & Frequency
grammar_focus: Connectors (and, but, because, so, although) & adverbs of frequency
vocabulary_focus: Sequencers (first, then, after that, finally), routine habits
pronunciation_focus: Pausing and rhythm after discourse connectors
desc: Stop speaking in choppy short sentences by linking ideas smoothly.
warmup_prompt: Why did you decide to improve your English?
roleplay_scenario: Telling the story of a funny or stressful travel experience from start to finish.
objectives: Use 'because' (reason) vs 'so' (result) without mixing them up
Place frequency adverbs (always, usually, rarely) in the right position
Tell a 4-step story using 'first, then, after that, finally'
communicative_function: Stop speaking in choppy short sentences by linking ideas smoothly.

title: Making Invitations & Polite Refusals
grammar_focus: Would you like to...?, Let's..., How about + -ing?
desc: Invite people out, accept enthusiastically, or say no politely with a reason.
warmup_prompt: Do you prefer staying in or going out on Friday nights?
roleplay_scenario: Inviting a colleague for lunch and rescheduling when they are busy.
objectives: Use 'How about going...' (+ -ing) and 'Would you like to...'
Refuse politely ('I'd love to, but...', 'Maybe another time')
Propose an alternative day and time
communicative_function: Invite people out, accept enthusiastically, or say no politely with a reason.

title: Hotel Check-in & Solving Travel Problems
grammar_focus: Polite indirect requests ('Could you...', 'Is it possible to...')
vocabulary_focus: Reservations, room amenities, complaints, Wi-Fi/AC issues
desc: Check into a hotel and politely ask to fix a problem with your room.
warmup_prompt: What makes a hotel stay great or terrible for you?
roleplay_scenario: Checking into a hotel where the Wi-Fi isn't working and the room is noisy.
objectives: Confirm reservation details (nights, breakfast, checkout)
Explain a problem calmly without sounding rude
Request a room change or technician politely
communicative_function: Check into a hotel and politely ask to fix a problem with your room.

title: A2 Milestone: Connected Speech & Review
grammar_focus: Mixed A2 tenses (Present, Past Simple, Going to/Will) & articles (a/an/the)
vocabulary_focus: High-frequency everyday expressions and fillers (well, actually, by the way)
desc: Consolidate everything in A2 with a realistic multi-topic conversation.
warmup_prompt: What has been easiest or hardest for you in English so far?
roleplay_scenario: A 10-minute coffee chat covering your past week, current job, and next vacation plans.
objectives: Switch smoothly between past, present, and future tenses
Use 'a/an/the' accurately in common nouns
Speak with fewer pauses using natural fillers
communicative_function: Consolidate everything in A2 with a realistic multi-topic conversation.

title: Life Experiences (Present Perfect vs. Past Simple)
grammar_focus: Present Perfect (have/has + V3) with ever/never vs. Past Simple for specific times
pronunciation_focus: Contractions 'I've / you've / she's' and past participles
desc: Master when to use 'I have been' versus 'I went' when sharing experiences.
warmup_prompt: Have you ever traveled to another country or met someone famous?
roleplay_scenario: Playing 'Two Truths and a Lie' about life experiences and asking follow-up questions.
objectives: Start with Present Perfect ('Have you ever...?') and switch to Past Simple for details ('When did you...?')
Avoid using Present Perfect with finished time words like 'yesterday'
Use 'never', 'already', and 'yet' naturally
communicative_function: Master when to use 'I have been' versus 'I went' when sharing experiences.

title: Duration & Ongoing Habits (Present Perfect Continuous)
grammar_focus: Present Perfect Continuous (have been + -ing) with 'for' and 'since'
vocabulary_focus: Work projects, learning journeys, hobbies over time
desc: Talk about how long you have been doing things that started in the past and continue now.
warmup_prompt: How long have you been working in your current field or studying English?
roleplay_scenario: Catching up with an old friend after 2 years and sharing what you've been up to.
objectives: Use 'for' (period of time) vs 'since' (starting point) accurately
Avoid saying 'I am working here since 2022' — use 'I've been working'
Ask 'How long have you been...?' questions
communicative_function: Talk about how long you have been doing things that started in the past and continue now.

title: Real & Hypothetical Situations (1st & 2nd Conditionals)
grammar_focus: 1st Conditional (If + present, will) vs. 2nd Conditional (If + past, would)
desc: Discuss realistic future consequences and imaginary 'what if' scenarios.
warmup_prompt: If you won a free year off work with full pay, what would you do?
roleplay_scenario: Evaluating a job offer in another city and weighing pros, cons, and 'what ifs'.
objectives: Avoid putting 'will' or 'would' inside the 'if' clause
Distinguish real plans (1st) from imaginary dreams (2nd)
Use 'If I were you, I would...' to give advice
communicative_function: Discuss realistic future consequences and imaginary 'what if' scenarios.

title: Modals of Deduction & Problem Solving
grammar_focus: Modals of probability (must be, might/could be, can't be) & advice (should have)
pronunciation_focus: Stress on modal verbs to show certainty
desc: Make smart guesses about situations when you don't have 100% of the facts.
warmup_prompt: If a coworker is 30 minutes late and not answering messages, what might have happened?
roleplay_scenario: Solving a workplace mystery where an important client file went missing.
objectives: Use 'must be' (95% sure) vs 'might/could be' (50% sure) vs 'can't be' (impossible)
Express polite disagreement with a theory
Propose next steps clearly
communicative_function: Make smart guesses about situations when you don't have 100% of the facts.

title: Describing Things Clearly (Relative Clauses)
grammar_focus: Defining relative clauses (who, which, that, where, whose)
pronunciation_focus: Smooth phrasing without unnatural pauses before 'who/that'
desc: Explain any word you forget in English by describing it with relative clauses.
warmup_prompt: What is an app that you use every single day?
roleplay_scenario: A 'Taboo'-style game where you describe objects, jobs, and places without saying their names.
objectives: Use 'who' for people, 'which/that' for things, 'where' for places
Paraphrase around unknown vocabulary smoothly
Avoid repeating the pronoun ('the man who he works...' -> 'the man who works...')
communicative_function: Explain any word you forget in English by describing it with relative clauses.

title: Narrative Tenses & Storytelling
grammar_focus: Past Simple + Past Continuous + Past Perfect (had + V3)
desc: Tell engaging stories where events happened in different moments of the past.
warmup_prompt: Tell me about a time you arrived somewhere and realized you had forgotten something.
roleplay_scenario: Sharing a memorable movie plot or a surprising personal story.
objectives: Use Past Perfect ('had already left') to show an earlier past action
Maintain listener interest with vivid adjectives
Sequence events logically
communicative_function: Tell engaging stories where events happened in different moments of the past.

title: Processes & News (Intro to Passive Voice)
grammar_focus: Passive Voice in Present and Past Simple (is made, was built, has been updated)
desc: Focus on what happened or how something is made when the action matters more than who did it.
warmup_prompt: What is a famous product or food that is made in your region?
roleplay_scenario: Explaining how a project, app, or product is built and tested at work.
objectives: Form Present/Past Passive ('be' + past participle) accurately
Use 'by' only when the agent is important
Describe a 3-step process clearly
communicative_function: Focus on what happened or how something is made when the action matters more than who did it.

title: Essential Phrasal Verbs in Action
grammar_focus: Separable vs. inseparable phrasal verbs (figure out, put off, look up, give up)
pronunciation_focus: Stressing the particle in phrasal verbs (turn OFF, pick UP)
desc: Sound much more natural by replacing formal Latinate verbs with everyday phrasal verbs.
warmup_prompt: What is something difficult you almost gave up on, but figured out?
roleplay_scenario: Discussing work habits, procrastination, and solving a technical hiccup.
objectives: Use 5+ common phrasal verbs naturally in conversation
Place pronouns correctly ('turn it off', not 'turn off it')
Recognize phrasal verb meanings from context
communicative_function: Sound much more natural by replacing formal Latinate verbs with everyday phrasal verbs.

title: Expressing Opinions & Polite Disagreement
grammar_focus: Opinion frames (In my view, As far as I'm concerned, On the other hand)
vocabulary_focus: Remote work, AI, lifestyle, social media
pronunciation_focus: Softening tone when disagreeing ('I see your point, however...')
desc: Share your point of view clearly, give reasons, and disagree respectfully.
warmup_prompt: Do you think remote work is better than working in an office?
roleplay_scenario: A friendly debate on remote work vs. office collaboration.
objectives: Move beyond 'I think' — use 3+ opinion phrases
Acknowledge the other person's point before disagreeing
Support opinions with 'for example' and 'because of that'
communicative_function: Share your point of view clearly, give reasons, and disagree respectfully.

title: B1 Milestone: Tech & Career Interview
grammar_focus: Integration of B1 tenses, conditionals, and modals
pronunciation_focus: Confident pacing and clear sentence endings
desc: Put all B1 skills together in a realistic screening interview.
warmup_prompt: How would you summarize your professional background in 30 seconds?
roleplay_scenario: A 1-on-1 international screening call discussing your experience, a past challenge, and future goals.
objectives: Answer 'Tell me about yourself' clearly and concisely
Describe a past problem you solved using narrative tenses
Ask 2 smart questions about the role
communicative_function: Put all B1 skills together in a realistic screening interview.

title: Regrets & Alternate Realities (3rd & Mixed Conditionals)
grammar_focus: 3rd Conditional (If + had V3, would have V3) & Mixed Conditionals
vocabulary_focus: Decisions, hindsight, turning points, lessons learned
pronunciation_focus: Fast reduction of 'would have' (/ˈwʊdəv/) and 'should have' (/ˈʃʊdəv/)
desc: Reflect on past decisions and how they would change the present.
warmup_prompt: If you hadn't chosen your current career, what would you be doing today?
roleplay_scenario: Analyzing a famous business mistake or personal turning point.
objectives: Form 3rd and Mixed Conditionals without 'would have' in the if-clause
Use 'should have / shouldn't have' for past criticism/regret
Pronounce 'would've / could've' smoothly
communicative_function: Reflect on past decisions and how they would change the present.

title: Reported Speech & Summarizing Conversations
grammar_focus: Reported statements, questions, and reporting verbs (claimed, warned, suggested)
desc: Accurately report what a client, manager, or friend told you.
warmup_prompt: What is the best piece of advice someone ever gave you?
roleplay_scenario: Debriefing your manager after a tense meeting with a client.
objectives: Apply tense backshifting naturally when appropriate
Use 'ask if / wonder whether' with statement word order in reported questions
Replace 'said' with richer reporting verbs (advised, insisted, promised)
communicative_function: Accurately report what a client, manager, or friend told you.

title: Advanced Passive & Causatives
grammar_focus: Passive across tenses + Causative 'have/get something done'
pronunciation_focus: Stress on the past participle in causatives
desc: Distinguish between doing something yourself and arranging for someone else to do it.
warmup_prompt: When was the last time you had something repaired or professionally done?
roleplay_scenario: Managing a home renovation or product launch with external contractors.
objectives: Use 'have/get + object + past participle' naturally
Use passive modals ('needs to be fixed', 'should have been tested')
Give crisp, professional status updates
communicative_function: Distinguish between doing something yourself and arranging for someone else to do it.

title: Debating Complex Issues (Discourse Markers)
grammar_focus: Contrast & concession markers (whereas, despite, in spite of, nevertheless, even though)
desc: Structure persuasive, balanced arguments on modern societal topics.
warmup_prompt: Despite the convenience of AI, what is one risk you worry about?
roleplay_scenario: A structured mini-debate on technology regulation or urban sustainability.
objectives: Use 'despite + noun/-ing' vs 'although + clause' accurately
Present a counterargument before refuting it
Avoid overusing 'but' by varying linkers
communicative_function: Structure persuasive, balanced arguments on modern societal topics.

title: Nuanced Verbs: Gerunds vs. Infinitives
grammar_focus: Verbs that change meaning (remember/forget/stop/regret/try + -ing vs. to + V)
desc: Master subtle meaning differences like 'stop smoking' vs. 'stop to smoke'.
warmup_prompt: Have you ever tried learning something unusual just to see if you liked it?
roleplay_scenario: Discussing productivity habits, mistakes, and lessons learned at work.
objectives: Contrast 'remember doing' (memory) vs 'remember to do' (task)
Contrast 'try doing' (experiment) vs 'try to do' (effort)
Use prepositions + gerund ('look forward to meeting', 'insist on paying')
communicative_function: Master subtle meaning differences like 'stop smoking' vs. 'stop to smoke'.

title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses & Precision
grammar_focus: Non-defining clauses (', which...', ', who...') & sentence-level ', which means...'
pronunciation_focus: Brief comma-pause intonation before and after non-defining clauses
desc: Add extra commentary and nuance smoothly inside complex spoken sentences.
warmup_prompt: Tell me about a tool or habit that changed your workflow, and why.
roleplay_scenario: Presenting a product or city profile to an executive audience.
objectives: Use ', which...' to comment on an entire previous clause
Never use 'that' in non-defining clauses
Use vocal pauses to separate extra info cleanly
communicative_function: Add extra commentary and nuance smoothly inside complex spoken sentences.

title: Business Negotiations & Diplomatic English
grammar_focus: Softeners & hedging (tend to, seems like, would it be possible, I'm afraid...)
desc: Negotiate deadlines, scope, or compensation firmly yet diplomatically.
warmup_prompt: How do you usually say 'no' to an unrealistic deadline?
roleplay_scenario: Negotiating project scope and timeline with a demanding stakeholder.
objectives: Soften direct refusals with 'I'm afraid...' or 'While I understand...'
Propose conditional trade-offs ('If we extend X, we can deliver Y')
Summarize agreed action items clearly
communicative_function: Negotiate deadlines, scope, or compensation firmly yet diplomatically.

title: B2 Milestone: Spontaneous Fluency & Idioms
grammar_focus: Full B2 grammar range + natural idiomatic expressions
vocabulary_focus: Idioms (on the same page, cut corners, blessing in disguise, silver lining)
pronunciation_focus: Connected speech, elision, and natural rhythm
desc: Speak spontaneously on unexpected topics with B2 fluency and self-correction.
warmup_prompt: Have you ever had a setback that turned out to be a blessing in disguise?
roleplay_scenario: A dynamic podcast-style interview covering career, culture, and current trends.
objectives: Speak at length without losing grammatical control
Self-correct minor slips spontaneously
Use 3+ natural idioms in context
communicative_function: Speak spontaneously on unexpected topics with B2 fluency and self-correction.

title: Persuasive Emphasis (Inversion & Cleft Sentences)
grammar_focus: Negative inversion (Not only did..., Rarely have I...) & Clefts (What I need is...)
desc: Elevate your speaking from clear to compelling using high-level emphasis structures.
warmup_prompt: What is something that surprised you most about your industry?
roleplay_scenario: Delivering a persuasive pitch to convince a board to adopt a new strategy.
objectives: Use 'Not only did X, but also Y' with correct auxiliary inversion
Use 'What really matters is...' cleft sentences for focus
Maintain natural flow without sounding robotic
communicative_function: Elevate your speaking from clear to compelling using high-level emphasis structures.

title: Advanced Hypotheticals (Wish, If Only, It's Time)
grammar_focus: Wish/If only + past/past perfect/would; It's high time + past; I'd rather + past
pronunciation_focus: Expressive intonation for wishes and frustration
desc: Express nuanced wishes, regrets, and polite urgencies with native-like precision.
warmup_prompt: What is one thing in modern education or tech you wish worked differently?
roleplay_scenario: Critiquing a flawed system and proposing realistic reforms.
objectives: Distinguish 'wish + past' (present) from 'wish + had V3' (past) and 'wish + would' (annoyance)
Use 'It's high time we addressed...'
Use 'I'd rather you didn't...' accurately
communicative_function: Express nuanced wishes, regrets, and polite urgencies with native-like precision.

title: Executive & Academic Hedging, Ellipsis
grammar_focus: Hedging (arguably, ostensibly, to some extent) & Ellipsis/Substitution (so/not, do so)
desc: Avoid overgeneralizations and repetition by using sophisticated academic/executive phrasing.
warmup_prompt: To what extent do you think automation will reshape knowledge work?
roleplay_scenario: Analyzing a complex market trend in an executive roundtable.
objectives: Qualify claims with hedging language instead of absolutes
Use substitution ('I hope so', 'if not', 'to do so') to avoid repetition
Synthesize two opposing viewpoints concisely
communicative_function: Avoid overgeneralizations and repetition by using sophisticated academic/executive phrasing.

title: C1 Milestone: Ethics, AI & Abstract Debate
grammar_focus: Participle clauses, advanced passives ('is thought to have...'), register shifting
desc: Defend complex, abstract positions under challenging follow-up questioning.
warmup_prompt: Where should we draw the line between convenience and privacy?
roleplay_scenario: A high-level panel discussion on ethics in artificial intelligence.
objectives: Handle unexpected counterarguments smoothly
Shift register between formal analysis and relatable examples
Use participle clauses ('Having considered the risks...')
communicative_function: Defend complex, abstract positions under challenging follow-up questioning.

title: Rhetorical Precision, Nuance & Subtle Humor
grammar_focus: Understatement, litotes, complex appositives, stylistic inversion
vocabulary_focus: Low-frequency idioms, cultural references, tone modulation
pronunciation_focus: Subtle irony, dry humor, and micro-intonation
desc: Master the subtleties of tone, understatement, and wit in high-level English.
warmup_prompt: What cultural differences in humor or politeness have you noticed in English?
roleplay_scenario: An engaging salon-style conversation on art, media, and modern absurdities.
objectives: Use British/American understatement and nuanced qualifiers
Read and respond to subtle tonal shifts
Express complex ideas effortlessly with zero hesitation
communicative_function: Master the subtleties of tone, understatement, and wit in high-level English.

title: Cross-Cultural Diplomacy & High-Stakes Synthesis
grammar_focus: Full mastery of register, strategic ambiguity, and persuasive framing
desc: Navigate sensitive, high-stakes conversations with complete linguistic command.
warmup_prompt: How do you reframe a controversial failure into a constructive path forward?
roleplay_scenario: Leading a sensitive international stakeholder alignment meeting after a major setback.
objectives: De-escalate tension using diplomatic reframing
Synthesize competing priorities into a unified narrative
Demonstrate near-native lexical precision
communicative_function: Navigate sensitive, high-stakes conversations with complete linguistic command.

title: Shopping, Prices & Numbers
grammar_focus: This/That/These/Those + 'How much is/are...?'
communicative_function: Asking for prices, sizes, and paying at a store
desc: Ask how much items cost, choose colors/sizes, and pay at a shop.
warmup_prompt: What did you buy most recently?
roleplay_scenario: Buying a gift at a souvenir or clothing shop.
objectives: Use 'How much is this?' vs 'How much are these?'
Pronounce numbers 13-90 clearly
Complete a polite purchase

title: Yesterday with Was & Were
grammar_focus: Past Simple of 'to be' (was / were / wasn't / weren't)
communicative_function: Describing where you were and how things were in the past
vocabulary_focus: Past time markers (yesterday, last night), weather & mood adjectives
pronunciation_focus: Weak vs strong forms of was/were
desc: Take your first step into the past tense using 'was' and 'were'.
warmup_prompt: Where were you yesterday evening?
roleplay_scenario: Talking about a recent concert, dinner, or weekend trip.
objectives: Use 'was' (I/he/she/it) and 'were' (you/we/they) accurately
Ask 'Were you...?' and 'How was it?'
